notice: The official site emergency plan always takes priority. Use this hub to prepare, practise and record. In a real emergency, follow the site plan and call the emergency number for your country.

plan_sections.title: 1. Site description and hazards
plan_sections.hint: Address, layout, number of people per shift, visitors and contractors, main hazards such as fuel, chemicals, gases, hot work, heights, neighbours.

plan_sections.title: 2. Emergency organisation
plan_sections.hint: Who is the Incident Controller and deputy, fire wardens, first aiders, rescue team and muster coordinator for each shift. Include night and weekend cover.

plan_sections.title: 3. Alarm and communication
plan_sections.hint: How the alarm sounds, who calls the emergency services, radio channels, public address, phone tree and how contractors are told.

plan_sections.title: 4. Evacuation routes and muster points
plan_sections.hint: Exit routes from every area, assembly points, wind direction, who does the headcount, how visitors and contractors are counted.

plan_sections.title: 5. Emergency services and outside help
plan_sections.hint: Emergency numbers, site access gate, who meets the services, the site map and hazard information to hand over.

plan_sections.title: 6. Emergency scenarios
plan_sections.hint: Fire, chemical spill, toxic gas release, medical emergency, confined space rescue, severe weather and flood. Say who does what in the first 5 minutes.

plan_sections.title: 7. Emergency equipment
plan_sections.hint: Extinguishers, hydrants, eyewash and showers, first aid, spill kits, breathing apparatus, stretchers, AED and where each is kept.

plan_sections.title: 8. Medical response
plan_sections.hint: First aiders, nearest hospital and best route, ambulance access, trauma kit and AED location.

plan_sections.title: 9. Training and drills
plan_sections.hint: Drill schedule, who attends, how records are kept, contractor induction on emergency arrangements.

plan_sections.title: 10. Review and approval
plan_sections.hint: Review date, who approved the plan, revision number and what changed.

roles.label: Incident Controller
duties: Takes charge and decides evacuation or stand-down
Keeps a log of times and decisions
Meets the emergency services and hands over site information
Declares the all clear

roles.label: Fire / Area Warden
duties: Sweeps the area and closes doors
Directs people to the nearest safe exit
Reports missing people to the muster coordinator
Wears the warden vest

roles.label: First Aider
duties: Goes to the casualty with the first aid kit and AED
Gives first aid within their training
Hands over to the ambulance crew with a clear report

roles.label: Rescue Team Leader
duties: Checks the rescue plan, equipment and the team
Never allows entry without breathing apparatus where needed
Keeps the team members within their training

roles.label: Muster Coordinator
duties: Holds the muster list and does the headcount
Reports the numbers and missing names to the Incident Controller
Keeps everyone at the muster point until released

roles.label: Communications Officer
duties: Calls the emergency services and the site management
Uses the radio channel and phone tree
Informs client, authorities and families as the plan says

roles.label: Gate / Security
duties: Keeps the access road clear for emergency vehicles
Directs responders to the incident
Controls entry and records who arrives

muster_guidelines: Choose at least two muster points in different directions
Place them upwind, away from buildings, fuel, gas and process areas
Keep them clear of emergency vehicle routes
Mark them with large signs that can be seen from every work area
Keep a muster board, forms and pens, hi-vis vests and torches at each point
Include a way to count contractors and visitors
Tell every worker which muster point to use from their area

scenarios.title: Fire
first_minutes: Raise the alarm and call the emergency number
Rescue people in immediate danger only if it is safe
Close doors and windows to slow the fire
Fight a small fire only if trained and your exit is behind you
Evacuate to the muster point and report to the warden
Do not use lifts. Do not go back for belongings
inform: Neighbouring sites if smoke or fire may spread
dont: Do not fight a large or spreading fire
Do not use water on oil, gas or electrical fires
Do not block exits or the access road
Do not re-enter until the all clear

drill.objective: Raise the alarm, evacuate everyone and complete the headcount.
prompts: Did everyone hear the alarm in every area?
Were any exits blocked or locked?
Did contractors and visitors know what to do?
Was anyone missing or slow to leave?
Did the wardens report correctly?

scenarios.title: Chemical or oil spill
first_minutes: Raise the alarm and warn people nearby
Stay upwind and keep away from the spill
Stop the source if it is safe (close valve, upright container)
Remove ignition sources and stop work nearby
Contain the spill with the spill kit and cover drains
Get help for anyone splashed: eyewash or shower for at least 15 minutes
inform: Emergency services if there is fire, injury or release off site
Environmental authority where the law requires
dont: Do not touch the spill without the right PPE
Do not wash a spill into the drain
Do not mix absorbents or neutralisers without checking the SDS

drill.objective: Contain a spill, protect people and call for help.

events.label: Area isolated and ignition sources removed
Headcount of people in the area

prompts: Did people know the chemical and its hazards?
Was the spill kit complete and easy to reach?
Were drains covered quickly?
Did the person with a splash get to the eyewash fast?

scenarios.title: Toxic gas release (H2S, ammonia, chlorine)
first_minutes: Sound the gas alarm
Move crosswind then upwind away from the release, to the upwind muster point
Put on escape breathing apparatus if you have it
Do not run in to rescue anyone without breathing apparatus
Isolate the source only if safe and trained
Rescue team goes in with SCBA and a plan
dont: Never trust your sense of smell
Never enter the gas area to rescue without breathing apparatus
Never go to a downwind muster point

drill.objective: Reach the upwind muster point and confirm everyone is accounted for.

events.label: Everyone at the upwind muster point
Rescue team ready with breathing apparatus

prompts: Did everyone go upwind?
Were escape sets within reach and used correctly?
Was anyone working alone and missed?
Was the wind direction obvious?

scenarios.title: Serious injury or medical emergency
first_minutes: Make the area safe and stop the cause
Call the emergency number and the site first aider
Check responsiveness and breathing
Start CPR and use the AED if the person is not breathing normally
Control serious bleeding with firm pressure
Send someone to meet the ambulance at the gate
dont: Do not move a person with a suspected spine injury unless in danger
Do not give food or drink
Do not leave the casualty alone
equipment: Trauma kit and tourniquet where trained

drill.objective: Get a first aider and AED to the casualty fast and hand over to the ambulance.
prompts: How fast did the first aider arrive?
Was the AED easy to find and ready?
Did someone meet the ambulance?
Was the report to the crew clear?

scenarios.title: Confined space rescue
first_minutes: Attendant raises the alarm and stays at the entrance
Do not enter to rescue without breathing apparatus and a rescue plan
Call the rescue team and the emergency services
Rescue team checks the atmosphere and the plan before entry
Use the retrieval line and rescue equipment
Hand the casualty to the first aiders and ambulance
dont: Never let an untrained person enter to rescue
Never cancel the alarm before the casualty is out and checked

drill.objective: Reach and remove a casualty from a confined space safely.
prompts: Did the attendant stay out and raise the alarm?
Was the rescue plan followed?
Was the equipment ready outside the space?
Did anyone try to enter without breathing apparatus?

scenarios.title: Flood, storm or extreme weather
first_minutes: Stop outdoor and high-risk work: cranes, lifting, work at height
Move people away from low areas, trenches and temporary structures
Isolate power in flooded areas and shut down generators in water
Secure loose materials and equipment
Account for everyone and check on lone workers
Watch for displaced snakes, insects and damaged services
inform: Workers in the camp or hostel
Neighbours and utilities if services are damaged
dont: Do not walk or drive through flood water
Do not touch electrical equipment in water
Do not restart work until the area is checked as safe

drill.objective: Stop work, move people to safe areas and complete a headcount.
prompts: How did the warning reach everyone including contractors?
Were trenches and lifts stopped fast?
Was anyone working alone and missed?
Was power isolated safely?

drill_targets.note: Suggested targets. Set your own in the site plan.

items.text: Kit is sealed, in its place and easy to reach
Items are complete and in date
AED is in its place, charged and pads are in date
items.fail: Service the AED or replace pads

items.text: Stretcher and burn dressings available
First aider list and numbers are posted and current
Unit is clear, signed and within 10 seconds of the hazard
Flush test: water runs clear and flows on both eyes
Dust covers in place and water is tepid
items.fail: Fix covers or the water supply

items.text: Portable bottles are in date and sealed
Kit is sealed and placed near the hazard
Absorbents, bags, gloves and goggles complete
Drain covers or mats are available
Procedure card is inside the kit
Extinguishers pass the monthly check (see Fire Safety)
items.fail: Tag out and replace the unit

items.text: Alarm call points and sounders tested this week
Emergency lighting and exit signs work
Hydrants, hose reels and fire blankets are accessible
Fire doors close fully and are not wedged open
SCBA cylinders are full and masks are clean and fit
Escape sets are in date and sealed
Tripod, winch, harness and rescue line are inspected
Gas detectors are calibrated and bump tested
Rescue team trained and list is current
Siren or alarm tested and audible in all areas
Radios charged and on the right channel
Phone tree and emergency numbers are current
Public address or megaphone works
Signs are visible and clean
Access is clear and upwind of hazards
Muster boards, forms, vests and torches are available
Contractor and visitor counting method is known
